samples.summary: A transient re-resolve failure now unmounts every mounted shared editor
samples.evidence: `SharedDocumentByToken` renders "Link unavailable" whenever `error` is truthy: `if (!token || error || !resolved)` (shared-document.tsx:1125). With `useQuery({ refetchInterval: 60_000, refetchOnWindowFocus: true, retry: 1 })`, a background refetch that fails twice sets `error` while `data` (the previously resolved link) is still cached — react-query keeps `data` on a refetch failure — so the branch fires and `SharedDocumentInner` (shared-document.tsx:1139) unmounts. That tears down consumers the diff never shows: the `DocumentProvider`/`YorkieProvider` subtree at shared-document.tsx:1011-1074, the mounted docs/slides/notes/board/sheet editor and its store, presence, in-flight image uploads and any open composer/IME state — for what may be a 2-attempt network blip, replacing a working session with an error page until the next interval tick. Before this change a resolve error could only happen before the first mount. Guarding the error branch on `!resolved` (i.e. only when there is no usable link) would keep the tighten-the-role behaviour without evicting a live session.

samples.summary: Undo floor now depends on `getUndoStackForTest()` returning identity-stable entries
samples.evidence: `canUndo()` was changed to `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark) < stack.length - 1` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2997-3004), which only works if the SDK's `getUndoStackForTest()` hands back the live stack (or at least the same inner entry objects) on every call. It is a `...ForTest` accessor, i.e. explicitly not a stable public contract, and the SDK is not vendored in this tree so I could not confirm it. If it ever returns copied entries, `lastIndexOf` is always `-1`, `canUndo()` answers `true` for the initial-load prefix, and a user can undo past `setDocument()` — the exact destruction the floor exists to prevent (the write it undoes is `writeFullDocument`, and the cursor still references blocks it removes). The old `length > undoFloor` comparison could not fail that way. Worth pinning with a test that asserts a floor-only stack reports `canUndo() === false` through this new code path (the added test only covers the overflow direction).

samples.summary: NotesView now rebuilds its store per `readOnly` flip but never releases the store's document subscription
samples.evidence: `YorkieNoteStore`'s constructor subscribes to the document and discards the unsubscribe handle (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:143), and the class exposes no `dispose()`. The NotesView cleanup only disposes the editor and nulls the ref (notes-view.tsx:150-155). Adding `readOnly` to the deps (notes-view.tsx:167) means every downgrade constructs another store while the Yorkie document — owned by the enclosing provider — stays attached, so each rebuild leaves a subscriber attached to a dead store forever. This is precisely the leak the diff fixed for docs by adding `YorkieDocStore.dispose()` and calling it (docs-view.tsx:574); slides already does the same (slides-view.tsx:1216). Notes is the one of the three left without it. Impact today is retention plus an accumulating `local-change` handler (it only writes to the orphaned store's own field), not wrong data.

samples.summary: Transient `new YorkieDocStore(doc)` in the import path is now the one site that skips the new `dispose()`
samples.evidence: `new YorkieDocStore(doc).setDocument(content.document)` (apply-imported-content.ts:224) constructs a store purely to write, then detaches the document at line 225. The constructor subscribes (`yorkie-doc-store.ts:632`), and this site keeps no reference, so the subscription is never released — while the sibling board branch three lines below does exactly that (`store.dispose()` at apply-imported-content.ts:235, with a comment explaining why). Now that `YorkieDocStore.dispose()` exists, this call site is out of step and should mirror the board branch.

samples.summary: The #1045 undo-floor bug is fixed only in the docs store; three sibling stores keep the depth comparison
samples.evidence: The diff replaces the depth-based floor with an identity mark in `YorkieDocStore.canUndo()`, on the grounds that Yorkie `shift()`s the oldest entry at the 50-entry cap. The same length-vs-depth comparison remains in `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:353` (`getUndoStackForTest().length > this.undoFloor`, with a comment at line 125 saying it "Mirrors YorkieDocStore.undoFloor" — now false), `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:654` and `packages/frontend/src/app/board/yorkie-board-store.ts:514`. Those surfaces still refuse reachable undos once the cap drops floor entries, and the notes comment now documents a contract the docs store no longer has.

samples.summary: Two render seams bypass the new "paint waits for the undo unit" hold
samples.evidence: The hold is implemented only in the `requestRender` wrapper (text-editor.ts:734-743). `requestCaretRender()` calls `(this.requestCursorRender ?? this.requestRender)()` (text-editor.ts:2981) and the layout-only path calls `(this.requestRenderNoCursorScroll ?? this.requestRender)()` (text-editor.ts:2268); when the host wires those optionals — the docs editor wires both (`view/editor.ts:2525`, and `requestRenderNoCursorScroll` elsewhere) — the call goes straight to the host and paints while the store batch is still open, defeating the invariant `withUndoUnit`'s doc comment states ("the screen always shows what the store really holds"). I could not find a current path that reaches either seam from inside a unit, so this is a latent bypass rather than a live one: the next mutating action that reuses `requestCaretRender` inside `withUndoUnit` gets a mid-batch paint with no signal. Routing both through the same depth check would close it.

finding.summary: A transient re-resolve failure now unmounts every mounted shared editor
finding.evidence: `SharedDocumentByToken` renders "Link unavailable" whenever `error` is truthy: `if (!token || error || !resolved)` (shared-document.tsx:1125). With `useQuery({ refetchInterval: 60_000, refetchOnWindowFocus: true, retry: 1 })`, a background refetch that fails twice sets `error` while `data` (the previously resolved link) is still cached — react-query keeps `data` on a refetch failure — so the branch fires and `SharedDocumentInner` (shared-document.tsx:1139) unmounts. verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. shared-document.tsx:1125 checks `error` before `resolved`, and the query at 1107-1119 uses refetchInterval/refetchOnWindowFocus with retry:1 against @tanstack/react-query v5 (package.json:56), which retains `data` on a failed background refetch while setting `error`. That makes the `error && resolved` state reachable on a transient API failure, short-circuiting before SharedDocumentInner (line 1139) and unmounting the YorkieProvider/CollabDocumentProvider subtree (lines 1011-1078) with its editors, presence and session-level analytics hook. resolveShareLink (api/share-links.ts:99-111) throws on any non-OK response, so the branch is not limited to genuine revocation, and no caller-side guard prevents it; the component is mounted long-lived from template-landing.tsx:174, template-review-queue.tsx:136 and the /shared/:token route. Impact lands on consumers outside the diff, so it is in-lane and blocking at major.

finding.summary: Undo floor now depends on `getUndoStackForTest()` returning identity-stable entries
finding.evidence: `canUndo()` was changed to `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark) < stack.length - 1` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2997-3004), which only works if the SDK's `getUndoStackForTest()` hands back the live stack (or at least the same inner entry objects) on every call. It is a `...ForTest` accessor, i.e. explicitly not a stable public contract, and the SDK is not vendored in this tree so I could not confirm it. If it ever returns copied entries, `lastIndexOf` is always `-1`, `canUndo()` answers `true` for the initial-load prefix, and a user can undo past `setDocument()` — the exact destruction the floor exists to prevent (the write it undoes is `writeFullDocument`, and the cursor still references blocks it removes). The old `length > undoFloor` comparison could not fail that way. Worth pinning with a test that asserts a floor-only stack reports `canUndo() === false` through this new code path (the added test only covers the overflow direction).

verdict.reason: The code is present as quoted (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2997-3005 uses lastIndexOf(undoFloorMark); markUndoFloor stores the top entry by identity at :885-888), but the failure mode the finding rests on is disproven by an existing test that runs against the real SDK. packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2,28 constructs a real `yorkie.Document` from `@yorkie-js/sdk` (pinned 0.7.20 in pnpm-lock.yaml:5689), and the test at :344-357 asserts `store.canUndo() === false` immediately after `setDocument()` (:348) and again after undoing the one mutation (:356). At both points `doc.history.canUndo()` is true (the beforeEach tree-creating update at :30-35 plus setDocument's own write are on the stack), so the early return at yorkie-doc-store.ts:2998 cannot yield that false — the assertion can only pass through the new `lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark)` branch at :3004. If the accessor did not return identity-stable entries, lastIndexOf would be -1, canUndo() would return true, and this test would fail. vite.config.ts:375-380 includes `tests/**/*.test.ts` in the vitest run, so the test is live. This also falsifies the finding's specific remediation claim that "the added test only covers the overflow direction": the floor-only assertion the reviewer asks for already exists at :344-357 (the overflow case at :365-386 is additional). Residual risk is limited to a hypothetical future SDK change to a pinned dependency, which this same test would catch; and the pre-change `length > undoFloor` form (still used at board/yorkie-board-store.ts:514, slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:654, notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:353) depended on the identical `...ForTest` accessor, so no new external dependency is introduced. Secondarily, the finding concerns the diff's own reliance on a third-party accessor rather than a caller left broken by the change, which sits with the correctness lens rather than blast-radius; but the refutation stands on the counterexample alone.
